page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmc5s.24xlarge is a compute-optimized bare-metal server instance operating on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processors operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz, this instance features 96 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 192 GB of system memory. This configuration establishes a strict 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 2.0 GB of memory per vCPU, tailored for workloads requiring significant multi-threaded parallel processing without demanding extensive per-core memory capacity.

The server provides a baseline network bandwidth of 32 Gbps, ensuring fast data transmission across distributed cloud environments and networked services. However, the instance includes no local storage or attached GPUs. Applications running on this node must rely entirely on remote network-attached block storage for persistence, which introduces reliance on external disk I/O performance. The absence of GPU acceleration restricts its applicability for hardware-accelerated machine learning training or real-time graphics rendering.

From an engineering perspective, the instance maximizes CPU core density and network throughput relative to memory footprint. This architecture offers distinct qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy parallel workloads that do not require massive RAM arrays or local ephemeral storage. Suitable workloads include high-concurrency web serving, large-scale software compilation, continuous integration and delivery pipelines, batch processing engines, and compute-bound simulation clusters.
